relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.role: Professor of Classical Indology and Religious Studies
relations.evidence: Axel Michaels (born 26 May 1949) is a Professor of Classical Indology and Religious Studies at Heidelberg University

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: After he completed his dissertation in 1978 summa cum laude, Michaels worked as a research assistant at the Museum of Ethnology in Hamburg

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: Michaels worked as a research assistant at the Museum of Ethnology in Hamburg and at the University of Münster.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: He then worked as an assistant professor at the Department of Indology at the University of Kiel (1980 until 1992)

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: meanwhile also holding the position as the Director of the Nepal Research Center (Kathmandu) from 1981 to 1983.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: From 1992 to 1996 Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Bern.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: In 1986, he was Spalding Visiting Fellow at the Wolfson College, Oxford.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: Since 1996, Michaels is professor of classical Indology at Heidelberg University’s South Asia Institute, which he managed as Director from 1999 to 2002.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: In 2002 he started a project in co-operation with Niels Gutschow which examined life cycle rituals in Nepal.

relations.subject: Axel Michaels
relations.evidence: shooting and production of the films Handling Death (2005) and Belfruit and loincloth (2007), realized in collaboration with Niels Gutschow and Christian Bau.
